title: Enterprise VPC: diagnose skewed per-token latency across model-fanout during regional failover
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: During an automated regional failover late 2025-03-10, a single enterprise VPC customer reported large divergence in per-token latency across model variants and regions. Initial triage shows first-token time (TTFT) increased ~2.5x for affected routes and sustained tokens/sec dropped by ~60% on requests that fan out to multi-variant backends. This appears specific to VPC/Dedicated routing paths and is reproducible when traffic is shifted off the primary region to a warm spare.
observed_metrics:
- TTFT baseline: 120ms -> observed median 300ms on failover
- Token throughput: 450 tokens/sec -> 180 tokens/sec for impacted node pool
- KV-cache miss rate: 4x increase (from 8% -> 32%)
- Kernel selection variance: worker groups A vs B selected different optimized kernels for the same model family (A: custom-int8, B: fp16-default)
impact_scope:
- A single Enterprise VPC customer (name redacted) experienced 10% of their API calls with degraded response time leading to customer SRE alerting.
- Hosted customers unaffected.
- Dedicated and Private pools in the failing region show degraded per-token performance when requests are routed to cross-region variants.
reproduction_steps:
1) Initiate canary regional failover by toggling route weight from primary to spare (test cluster: us-west-2 -> us-east-1).
2) Send synthetic fanout requests that hit model variants: base-1, base-1-int8, instruct-2.
3) Observe per-token latencies and KV cache hit metrics on the dedicated VPC worker pool.
4) Correlate kernel selection logs and model shard placement for the affected worker IDs.
initial_findings:
- Router routing table moved 28% of enterprise tenant traffic to cross-region pool that has a different kernel map.
- The spare pool had an older kernel build (selector heuristics v1.4.1 vs primary v1.5.0) which prioritized fp16 kernels; this increased memory pressure and amplified KV cache churn.
- Prefetch warmup only applied to primary region; warm spare lacked the recent warmup credits leading to more cold KV fetches.
- No application-level code changes on customer side; problem reproducible from internal test harness with tenant-scoped headers.
comments: 2025-03-10 23:12 - Ava Martinez: Incident reported by customer SRE; opening triage. Captured request IDs and preserved logs for affected sessions.

2025-03-11 02:03 - Rohit Singh: Reproduced locally by forcing routing weights to spare. Confirmed kernel map mismatch and high KV miss rate. Created a debug build with selector override to force primary kernel; provisional improvement noted (TTFT back to ~140ms).

2025-03-11 05:40 - Miguel Torres: Measured warmup credit discrepancy; spare pool had expired warmup tokens after recent cluster maintenance. Queued a warmup job to prepopulate prefix cache for the tenant.
2025-03-12 09:10 - Priya Nair (PM): Notified customer with interim mitigation steps and ETA for full fix. Customer accepted temporary routing pin to primary region while we investigate.

2025-03-13 16:22 - Rohit Singh: Validated that applying selector override on spare reduces KV miss to 12% and tokens/sec improves to ~380; still 15% slower than primary due to different quant path. Planning kernel selector roll-forward to spare nodes.
2025-03-14 10:00 - Ava Martinez: Outreach from security/compliance team requested to confirm no secrets crossed during routing; logs reviewed and no leakage found.
next_steps: Coordinate kernel-selector roll-forward to spare pool (runtime-1.22 hotpatch) and validate in canary; target 2025-03-15 for canary rollout.
Implement per-tenant warmup credits transfer during regional failover to ensure KV cache priming.
Add tracing to router to surface when kernel-map mismatches across pools and trigger automated fallback to compatible variant.
Run full replay test using customer's production prompt set to validate tokens/sec parity.
Prepare communication draft for affected customers if full rollout takes longer than 48 hours.
resolution_plan:
1) Immediate mitigation: Pin the enterprise tenant to primary region routing for outgoing requests (done 2025-03-11, reduces customer impact).
2) Short-term fix: Roll forward selector heuristics to spare pool (hotpatch runtime-1.22) and distribute warmup credits; verify via canary.
3) Long-term: Add router-level compatibility check to avoid cross-pool kernel mismatches and enhance warmup credit transfer during planned/unplanned failovers.
4) Postmortem to capture timeline, root cause (kernel selector drift + warmup credit expiry), and action items for preventing recurrence.
